notes: Dev-split TBox expansion paired with physics-replace-d005: gives a made-up class under a real one (fictional: subject), the Velkarin outburst, the revised rule's conclusion (has_progenitor: a brown dwarf). It cannot sit under Type II, nor under supernovae in general: every real Type II supernova comes from a massive star, and a supernova is by definition the explosion of a star (a massive one or a white dwarf), so a brown dwarf progenitor would override a held class rule (overwriting). It sits under a class of astronomical outbursts, which leaves the progenitor open. PHYSICALLY IMPOSSIBLE CONCLUSION: a brown dwarf never ignites hydrogen, so nothing known makes it explode; the insert contradicts no recorded fact about a named thing but goes against general stellar physics, as the revision does. Report this record apart. The prompts ask "what kind of object" because a brown dwarf is substellar, so the direct and paraphrase wording differs from d005's "star" on purpose. A made-up class has no members a model knows, so two derived questions follow the rule to the new conclusion and look up a stored fact about brown dwarfs (no hydrogen fusion in the core; the Sun is more massive; composition, 2 hops), and the third names an unnamed flash and asks what to look for in archival images (inheritance, application). Caveat: the two composition questions have likely default answers (a white dwarf progenitor also gives "no" and "yes"). The near unrelated question asks the progenitor of a Type II supernova (a massive star). The Crab Nebula side facts, checks and evidence are the revision's.
